name: Sampling

subjectOf.text: Enlarging the sample does not cure selection bias in non-statistical sampling: a bigger sample neither compensates for the bias of non-statistical techniques nor guarantees that the sample is representative.
subjectOf.abstract: Increasing the sample size does not necessarily compensate for the potential selection bias of non-statistical techniques or guarantee the representativeness of the sample.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Fund Disclosures Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2447306

subjectOf.text: GNN scalability on large real world graphs is a genuine trade off rather than an engineering gap: sampling methods lose influential neighbors while clustering methods lose structural patterns, so each remedy sacrifices part of the signal the model needs.
subjectOf.abstract: Scalability is a major concern for GNNs on large real-world graphs, as sampling methods may lose influential neighbors while clustering methods may lose structural patterns.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, How AI Models are Optimized Through Web3 Governance (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4855607
scope_conditions: large real world graphs where full graph processing is infeasible

subjectOf.text: A validity filter judges whether an output is correct rather than whether it is rare, so where rare content is as checkable as common content such a filter can change rare composition only through the generator's own error profile, and if collapse proceeds by under-sampling rare modes no validity filter restores them, a reputation-weighted filter included.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: The ceiling holds where rare content is as checkable as common content, which this design enforces by construction.
The experiment therefore includes an oracle validity filter as a premise rather than as a result.
